data.title: Woman with a Green Book (Louisa Gallond Cook)

thumbnail.alt_text: A work made of oil on canvas.

data.credit_line: Gift of the Estate of Edgar William and Bernice Chrysler Garbisch
data.publication_history:
Judith A. Barter, et al., American Arts at The Art Institute of Chicago: From Colonial Times to World War I (Art Institute of Chicago, 1998), 122, fig. 23.

Judith A. Barter and Monica Obniski, For Kith and Kin: The Folk Art Collection at the Art Institute of Chicago (Art Institute of Chicago/Yale University Press, 2012), 76-77, no. 28.
data.exhibition_history: Springfield, MA, Museum of Fine Arts, E.S. Field: Visionary Artist, Feb. 4–Apr. 1, 1984, cat. 62; traveled to Washington, DC, National Museum of American Art and National Portrait Gallery, June 10–Set.p 4, 1984.
data.provenance_text: Recorded as from Massachusetts. Thurston Thacher, the Rip Van Dam Shop, Hyde Park, New York, by 1952 [this and the following according to acquisition documents; copies in curatorial object file]; sold to Edgar William (1899–1979) and Bernice Chrysler Garbisch (1906–1979), New York and Pokety Farms, MD, May 13, 1952 [Garbisch Collection number 1952.30; on loan to the National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC, from Nov. 24, 1953 to 1980]; bequeathed to the Art Institute of Chicago, 1980.
